versions.changelog:
No presets, a preview that stays in view, and test messages in the Log

- Presets are gone. A new chat starts with every event on; switch off what you don't want. New kinds of event in later versions are added only to destinations that still have every event on. Upgrading keeps every destination's events as they are.
- In the bot, Add destination now sits in the Destinations screen as a blue button.
- Open in Telegram just opens the chat with the bot.
- The message preview stays in view under Jellyfin's header while you scroll.
- The Fields and Formatting tables keep their columns; long tags wrap instead of stretching the table.
- Test messages appear in the Log, labelled Test or Test failed.
- A group with topics is shown as a Forum.
- The sidebar counts are labels, the version in the header opens its release page, and Change token opens right where you pressed it.
- TgJelly sends at most two messages a second, to stay clear of Telegram's flood limits.

Messages on one page, a Log, and clearer everything

- Every status is a coloured label, like the Built-in and Edited badges. The release version sits next to TgJelly in the header.
- Messages and Templates are one page. Pick a message to see what it shows, its template and a preview that looks like Telegram.
- Message switches are per message now: posters on movies but not on episodes, for example. Security and Server messages can carry the TgJelly logo.
- Click a field or a format in the reference tables to insert it into the template. Hover a piece of the template to see what it produces in the preview, and the other way round.
- New Log section: every message, per destination, with what happened to it. Failed messages show Telegram's own words and what to do.
- Destinations show health only when something is wrong. Disconnecting the bot can also remove all destinations.
- Update checks: choose fixes, new releases and new major versions of Jellyfin separately, in the dashboard and in the bot.
- Proxy username and password appear only with a proxy. Diagnostics says exactly what the report contains.
- Every error says what happened and what to do.
- Upgrading from v0.4 keeps every message looking the same.

A new dashboard: sections, cards and auto-save

- The Telegram page is redesigned. A sidebar holds Overview, Destinations, Messages, Templates and Advanced, and becomes a row of tabs on a phone.
- Settings are grouped into cards with clear spacing and follow your Jellyfin theme.
- There are no Save buttons. Every setting saves itself, and "Saved" or "Not saved:" with the reason shows beside it.
- The public URL and proxy settings save when you leave the field or press Enter. Templates save a second after you stop typing, and never while they have errors.
- A change made in the bot while the dashboard is open is kept, and so is what you were typing.
- Destinations show their health in words, and switching away from a Custom preset asks first.
- Status in the bot now names your Jellyfin server.

Every message is a template, with a live preview editor

- Every notification now comes from a template. The built-in templates produce exactly the messages v0.2 sent.
- New Message templates section in the dashboard: see the template in use, change a word or a line, and watch a live Telegram-style preview as you type.
- Send test sends the template, saved or not, to any of your chats. Reset goes back to the built-in template.
- An edited template that breaks falls back to the built-in one, and the dashboard shows the error.
- Long messages are shortened the same way as before, for edited templates too.
- The templates guide lists every built-in template and explains how to change them.
- Upgrading from v0.2: a disabled custom template is dropped; an enabled one becomes your edited template.

Inline-only bot setup, icons and clearer screens

- Adding a destination is one inline message: Add to a channel, Add to a group or Right here. The add buttons open Telegram's own chat chooser, and setup continues in the same message.
- Chats the bot is already in are offered as "Set up <chat>".
- Topic creation permission is granted from a link button, with Check again.
- The public URL and topic link prompts use an inline Cancel button instead of a reply keyboard.
- Events are split into Media, Security and Server screens.
- Every bot screen explains what each of its buttons does.
- Custom emoji icons on buttons and headings. They show only if the bot owner has Telegram Premium.
- The dashboard shows the bot's name once, in the Bot section.

First test release

TgJelly sends Jellyfin events to Telegram chats, groups and channels through your own bot.

- New media, security and server events, with presets
- Setup from the bot with Telegram's chat picker, or from the dashboard
- Custom Scriban templates (Advanced)
- Builds for Jellyfin 10.11 (1.x) and 12 (2.x)

This is a pre-test release.

name: TgJelly
description: A Telegram bot inside your Jellyfin server: new media, security and server notifications for the chats, groups and channels you choose, set up from the dashboard or the bot.
